text: Stem nematode disease, commonly known internationally as ufra (ជំងឺកណ្មាតូដដើម), is caused by the nematode Ditylenchus angustus. It can cause yield losses of roughly 20–90% depending on severity. Early symptoms are small pale/white spots on young leaves, which enlarge and cause the leaf to droop downward; leaves may curl or twist, the plant tillers poorly, and the stem stays shortened. If the nematode reaches the plant during the booting stage, growth is stunted and the leaf sheath is deformed; panicles fail to fully emerge from the sheath, and the grain that does form is curled, malformed, and shrunken. The nematode lives in the soil and in plant residue. It infects a plant by reaching the growing point of a young tiller and moving with the plant's growth into new tissue. In older plants it goes dormant at the base of tillers and inside the leaf sheath; as the rice matures, the nematode curls up and survives in a dormant state on the stubble after harvest. The disease is worse where humidity is high and where a lot of infected plant residue is left in the field, and it spreads between fields through flowing irrigation water — deepwater fields are especially prone to this. Management: (1) keep fields clean — remove and destroy infected plant debris rather than leaving it in the field; (2) rotate rice with a different crop; (3) burn or plow under stubble right after harvest; (4) leave the field fallow/dry for 2–3 months before planting the next rice crop.
